NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.

NOV 22 1938

Opium-Smoking In
Prison
Cabaret Manager and Two
Warders Charged : Bribery
Alleged

The situation looks very bad for
Chen Tseng-hsiung, manager of the
An Lo Kwong Ballroom and Hotel
in Puc Ch' Pao San, popularly
known as "Blood Alley," for he
is charged with bribing warders of
the Second Special District Court
prison in order that he might have
more freedom in the jail where he
is to stay for six months on an
opium-smoking charge. When he
was brought before the tribunal on
Monday afternoon, the judge took so
serious a view of the case that he
refused to grant bail. Two other
prisoners and two warders also stood
trial but they all denied that they
were involved. Chen admitted hav-
ing bribed the warders. Judgment
will be passed on November 27.

The French police are still look-
ing for two fugitive warders believed
to have also been bribed in this ser-
ious case which has attracted so wide
attention among the Chinese that the
courtroom was crowded to capacity.
Chen readily admitted that he had
paid money to some warders in order
that he might be able to "obtain
boiled water" and cigarettes. His
lawyers asked for leniency stating
that their client's purpose of giving
money to warders was to reduce his
suffering and that his action did not
violate law. The judge refused to
grant their request for bail.

There was a heated debate between
the Chief Procurator, who drew up
the indictment against the accused,
and lawyers for the defence. The
procurator strongly urged the judge
to punish all accused, explaining that
despite their denial the accused
warders could not shift their respon-
sibility for receiving bribe money.
Lawyers speaking on behalf of the
accused warders did their best to
exonerate their clients, asserting that
the bribe money was received by the
warders who are at large.

Chen was sentenced many weeks
ago to six months' imprisonment and
during the imprisonment he was sup-
posed to get rid of his opium-smoking
habit. It was alleged, however, that
instead of trying to carry out the
order he asked the warders twice to
go to his hotel last month to obtain
money to buy things which serve no
purpose of the judge. The procura-
tor soon got wind of what had hap-
pened and drew up an indictment
charging him with bribery and the two
warders, with malfeasance in Office.
Two other prisoners were charged
with instigating the bribery.

1938年11月22日

监狱内的鸦片吸食
舞厅经理与两名狱警被控：涉嫌行贿

对于陈增雄（Chen Tseng-hsiung，音译）而言，局势看起来非常不妙。他是位于蒲石路（Puc Ch' Pao San，即今复兴中路一带，俗称“血巷”）安乐宫舞厅及酒店的经理。他被指控贿赂第二特区法院监狱的狱警，以便他在因吸食鸦片罪被判入狱六个月期间获得更大的自由。周一下午当他被带上法庭时，法官对此案看法极为严肃，拒绝准予保释。另外两名囚犯和两名狱警也一同受审，但他们均否认涉案。陈承认曾贿赂狱警。判决将于11月27日宣判。

法国警察仍在搜捕两名潜逃的狱警，据信他们也在这起引起华人广泛关注的严重案件中收受了贿赂，导致法庭内座无虚席。陈坦承他曾向某些狱警付款，以便能够“获得开水”和香烟。他的律师请求从轻发落，称其客户给狱警钱的目的是为了减轻痛苦，且其行为并未违法。法官拒绝了他们的保释请求。

起草对被告起诉书的主任检察官与辩护律师之间发生了激烈的辩论。检察官强烈敦促法官惩罚所有被告，解释说尽管被告狱警予以否认，但他们无法推卸收受贿款的责任。代表被告狱警发言的律师尽力为当事人开脱，声称贿款是由那些在逃的狱警收受的。

陈在数周前已被判处六个月监禁，在服刑期间本应戒除吸食鸦片的恶习。然而，据称他非但没有试图执行命令，反而在上个月两次要求狱警前往他的酒店取钱，用于购买与法官命令毫无关系的东西。检察官很快获悉了所发生的情况，并起草起诉书，指控他行贿，指控两名狱警渎职。另外两名囚犯被指控煽动行贿。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.

NOV 9    1939

Man Blackmailed
In Prison
Two Warders Abscond After
Extortion Attempt; Opium
Smoker Victim

Two warders of the Second Special
District Court Prison, who have fled
from their jobs, are being sought by
the French police while three
prisoners and another warder in the
same prison have been brought be-
fore the tribunal and detained in con-
nection with a bribery case in which
the three prisoners and warders are
alleged to have connived in extorting
$150, from a new inmate in the
prison.

The interest centres around Chen
Tseng-hsiung, proprietor of the An
Lo Kwung Ballroom in Rue Chu Pao
San, who was recently sentenced to
six months' imprisonment for smok-
ing opium. He was first ordered to
be sent to the detention quarters of
the court where he was to get rid of
his bad habit by undergoing a
medical treatment for a month. But
criminals are criminals and soon
Chen was preyed upon by other in-
mates of the jail choosing him as
their object of extortion.

Three other prisoners, Ching Chia-
chi, Tao Yung-chang and Chen Chiu-
sen, are alleged to have connived with
three warders and succeeded in
twice extorting money from the new
prisoner. It was hush money but the
chief warder soon got wind of what
had happened, and finally the matter
was brought to the attention of the
procurator who started the prosecu-
tion. Meanwhile two of the warders
fled.

When the case was again heard on
Monday afternoon, all the accused
tried to shift the responsibility of
the crime and the judge had to
postpone the hearing pending further
investigations. One of the prisoners
involved in the new case was once
sentenced to 10 years' imprisonment
charged with murder and was about
to be released while another one was
serving a one-year-and-six month
prison term on a charge of counter-
feiting.

1939年11月9日

监狱内的勒索案
两名狱警在企图敲诈后潜逃；一名鸦片吸食者成为受害者

第二特区法院监狱的两名狱警已逃离岗位，法国警察正在搜捕他们；与此同时，该监狱的三名囚犯和另一名狱警因一起贿赂案被带上法庭并拘留。据称，这三名囚犯和狱警合谋向监狱的一名新入狱者敲诈150元。

关注的焦点集中在陈增雄（Chen Tseng-hsiung，音译）身上，他是蒲石路（Rue Chu Pao San，即今复兴中路）安乐宫舞厅的老板，最近因吸食鸦片被判处六个月监禁。他最初被命令送往法院的拘留所，通过为期一个月的医疗治疗来戒除这一恶习。但是罪犯终究是罪犯，陈很快成为监狱中其他囚犯的猎物，被选为敲诈对象。

据称，另外三名囚犯——郑家基（Ching Chia-chi，音译）、陶永昌（Tao Yung-chang，音译）和陈秋森（Chen Chiu-sen，音译）——与三名狱警串通，成功两次从这名新囚犯那里敲诈钱财。这是一笔封口费，但首席狱警很快获悉了此事，最终将此事提请检察官注意，从而启动了公诉程序。在此期间，两名狱警潜逃。

当此案于周一下午再次开庭审理时，所有被告都试图推卸犯罪责任，法官不得不推迟听证，以待进一步调查。卷入这起新案件的一名囚犯曾因谋杀罪被判处十年监禁，即将获释；另一名囚犯则因伪造罪正在服一年六个月的刑期。

September 3, 1939. Morning Translation.

Sin Shun Pao (Japanese-owned Chinese language newspaper):

"FIRST SPECIAL DISTRICT COURT PRESIDENT ARRESTED
BY FRENCH POLICE FOR OPIUM TRAFFICKING"

Many corrupt practices have been committed by officials of the subordinate organs of the Kuomintang Government. Recently the President of the Shanghai First Special District Court in the French Concession (?) appointed by the Kuomintang Government of Chungking was discovered secretly selling confiscated opium. This affair took place at the time when a demand was being lodged for the return of the Courts in the Foreign Settlements.

On the night of August 31, whilst patrolling in the vicinity of Avenue Foch and Avenue du Roi Albert in the French Concession, a search party of the French Municipal Council noticed a strange motor car travelling at high speed without lights. When the car was about to turn into Avenue du Roi Albert, the search party stopped the car and the search resulted in the discovery of a large quantity of opium under the seats.

The chauffeur, a Chinese, upon being interrogated, stated that the opium was being transported to a certain place for secret sale on the instructions of Yang Chi (楊奇), age 38, the President of the Shanghai First Special District Court.

Upon receipt of this information, the French Municipal Council despatched officials to the private residence of Yang Chi on Route Stanislas Chevalier. There the officers found another large quantity of opium. Yang Chi was secretly escorted to the French Municipal Council and an investigation was started.

In transporting confiscated opium to his private residence for secret sale, Yang Chi was abusing his authority. It is believed that the investigation will involve many officials of the Court in the affair.

1939年9月3日。晨间译文。

《新顺报》（日资中文报纸）：

“第一特区法院院长因贩卖鸦片被法国警察逮捕”

国民党政府下属机构官员腐败行为频发。最近，由重庆国民党政府任命的上海法租界第一特区法院院长被发现秘密出售没收的鸦片。此事发生在要求归还外国租界内法院管辖权之际。

8月31日晚，法国公董局的一支搜查队在法租界福煦路（Avenue Foch）和阿尔贝王路（Avenue du Roi Albert）附近巡逻时，注意到一辆奇怪的汽车高速行驶且未开灯。当该车准备转入阿尔贝王路时，搜查队拦停了车辆，搜查结果在座位下发现了大量鸦片。

司机是一名中国人，在接受讯问时称，这些鸦片是奉上海第一特区法院院长、38岁的杨奇（Yang Chi）之命，运往某处进行秘密销售的。

收到此情报后，法国公董局派遣官员前往斯坦尼斯拉斯·谢瓦利埃路（Route Stanislas Chevalier，即今南昌路）杨奇的私宅。在那里，官员们又发现了大量鸦片。杨奇被秘密护送至法国公董局，调查随即展开。

杨奇将没收的鸦片运至私宅进行秘密销售，属于滥用职权。据信，调查将牵涉法院众多官员卷入此案。

Date September 4, 1939.
Subject Yang Chi (楊琦), President of the Shanghai Second Special District
Court, arrested by French Police.
Made by D.I. Fan Lien ih    Forwarded by C Grandio

Yang Chi (楊琦), President of the Shanghai
Second Special District Court (French Concession)
since April, 1939, was arrested by the French Police
at 7 a.m., August 31, 1939, for being concerned in
the unlawful disposal of opium which had been con-
fiscated by the Court. A considerable quantity of
such opium was seized from his residence at 90 Rue
Massenet. It is believed that his arrest was effected
after consultation with the Ministry of Justice of
the National Government at Chungking.

The unlawful activities of the President
were discovered on an arrest of a male Chinese, who
was found in possession of opium, by the French
Police on Avenue Foch. Interrogation of this arrest
revealed that the opium seized had been stolen from
a storehouse of the Court where the confiscated opium
was kept and that a substitute had been put in place
of the genuine opium. In consequence, the storehouse
keeper was also taken into custody by the French
Police. This case is being kept very confidential by
the French Police and further particulars are unavail-
able at present.

制作人：侦探督察 Fan Lien ih    转呈人：C Grandio

杨琦（楊琦），自1939年4月起担任上海第二特区法院（法租界）院长，于1939年8月31日上午7时被法国警察逮捕，原因是涉嫌非法处置由法院没收的鸦片。在其位于马思南路90号（90 Rue Massenet）的住所查获了大量此类鸦片。据信，此次逮捕是在与重庆国民政府司法部协商后执行的。

院长的非法活动是在法国警察于福煦路逮捕一名持有鸦片的中国男子时发现的。对该被捕者的讯问显示，被查获的鸦片是从存放没收鸦片的法院仓库中盗取的，并且用替代品替换了真鸦片。因此，仓库管理员也被法国警察拘留。法国警察对此案严格保密，目前暂无更多详情。

Court to relinquish post.

Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih. Forwarded by C. ____

With reference to Special Branch report of
December 3, 1938, on the above subject, Mr. Wong
Sze-muh (王恩默), President of the Shanghai Second
Special District Court who was dismissed by the
Ministry of Justice in November 1938 and refused to
hand over his post to his successor, has now given up
his defiant stand due it is reported, to persuasion
on the part of Mr. Yang Peng (楊鵬), President of
the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court, and the
French Consul-General. Mr. Wong handed over the reins
of office on or about February 28 to Mr. Yang Peng,
who now acts concurrently as President of the Shanghai
Second Special District Court as Mr. Yang Chi (楊琦),
the official appointed by the Government was recalled
to Chungking.

MAR 1 1950

Yang Peng Takes
Over Second Special
District Court Post

Mr. Yang Peng, Chief Judge of
the Third High Court, yesterday
officially assumed the concurrent
post of Chief Judge of the Second
Special District Court, pending the
arrival of the new appointee from
Chungking. Mr. Yang succeeds
Mr. Wang Shin-mo.

It is recalled that Mr. Wang
began winding up the affairs of
the court about three months ago
when an order came from Chung-
king, directing him to relinquish
the post.

A long-drawn-out squabble be-
tween Mr. Wang and the ap-
pointee, Mr. Yang Chi, resulted
after the former refused to give
up his office to the new arrival.

It was reported that when Mr.
Yang Chi posted a public notice
in front of the court house an-
nouncing his assumption of office,
Judge Wang, with his own hands,
tore down the notice and con-
tinued to function as judge of the
tribunal.

A settlement of the dispute was
not reached until the recall of
Mr. Yang Chi to Chungking by
the national authorities.

杨鹏接任
第二特区
法院职务

高等法院第三分院首席法官杨鹏先生，昨日正式兼任第二特区法院首席法官一职，以待重庆新任任命者到任。杨先生接替王 Shin-mo（王思默/王恩默，音译）先生。

回顾此前，约三个月前重庆下达命令，指示王先生离职，他便开始着手清理法院事务。

王先生与继任者杨琦先生之间旷日持久的争执，起因于前者拒绝向新到任者交出职位。

据报道，当杨琦先生在法院大楼前张贴公告宣布就职时，王法官亲手撕下公告，并继续履行法庭法官的职能。

直到国家当局将杨琦先生召回重庆，这场纠纷才得以解决。

November 25, 1938. Morning Translation

Standard and other local newspapers :-

THE NEW PRESIDENT OF THE SHANGHAI SECOND SPECIAL DISTRICT
COURT

Dr. Yang Chi (楊琦), M.A., a graduate of
"Lu Vang" University (魯文大學), France, who was formerly
Procurator of the Shanghai District Court and Chief
Procurator of the High Court at Kweichow, was recently
transferred as President of the Shanghai Second Special
District Court by order of the Ministry of Justice. He
arrived in Shanghai several days ago and as Mr. Wong Sze-
muh (王思默), the retiring President of the Second Special
District Court, is delaying the handing over of his post,
Dr. Yang wrote to Mr. Wong the other day informing him that
he would assume the post on November 24.
At about 9 a.m. yesterday Dr. Yang called on
Mr. Wong Sze-muh at the Second Special District Court and
explained the object of his call. Mr. Wong refused to hand
over the post. At 11.30 a.m. Dr. Yang instructed his men
to post up the following proclamation at the entrance of the
Court :-
"In compliance with Order No.1673 issued by
the Ministry of Justice appointing me as President of the
Shanghai Second Special District Court, I have assumed my
office as from this date. The ceremony of oath-taking
will take place later.
President Yang Chi,
November 24, 1938."
Dr. Yang also issued a circular memo to the
Judges of the Civil and Criminal Divisions informing them
of his assumption of office. At 11.40 a.m. he proceeded
to the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court to make a
similar report. Five minutes after Dr. Yang left his
office, Mr. Wong Sze-muh tore off the proclamation posted
by Dr. Yang.

Retiring President's Explanation

Mr. Wong Sze-muh is said to have made the
following statement :- "I have served in the Courts for
a number of years in the course of which I have never done
anything illegal and I have been loyal to the country.
Unexpectedly I have been dismissed by the Government. I am
not opposing the handing over of my post, but the procedure
adopted by Dr. Yang Chi to take over the post was irregular.
As I have held the present post for several years, many cases
have come through my hands and it is impossible to hand over
all these affairs in a short time. I am expediting the
handing over from to-day and I shall notify my superior to
detail an official to take over the office as soon as I have
settled all affairs. I shall not do anything harmful to the
country. In coming here to-day to take over the office, Dr.
Yang Chi was accompanied by Hsu San-long (許三郎). The
public should know what sort of man Hsu San-long is."

High Court Official Makes Statement

The following is a statement by a spokesman of
the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court:-
page_data.zh:
1938年11月25日。晨间译文

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：-

上海第二特区法院新院长

杨琦博士（楊琦），文学硕士，毕业于法国“鲁文大学”（Lu Vang University，魯文大學），曾任上海地方法院检察官及贵州高等法院首席检察官，近期奉司法部令调任上海第二特区法院院长。他于数日前抵达上海，鉴于第二特区法院离任院长王思默先生（王思默）拖延移交职位，杨博士日前致函王先生，告知其将于11月24日就职。
昨日上午9时许，杨博士前往第二特区法院拜访王思默先生，并说明来意。王先生拒绝移交职位。上午11时30分，杨博士指示其手下在法院入口处张贴如下公告：-
“遵照司法部第1673号令任命我为上海第二特区法院院长，我自即日起就职。宣誓仪式稍后举行。
院长 杨琦，
1938年11月24日。”
杨博士还向民事和刑事庭法官发出通函备忘录，通知他们其已就职。上午11时40分，他前往江苏高等法院第三分院作类似报告。杨博士离开办公室五分钟后，王思默先生撕毁了杨博士张贴的公告。

离任院长的解释

据说王思默先生发表了如下声明：“我在法院服务多年，期间从未做过任何违法之事，且对国家忠诚。未曾想竟被政府免职。我并非反对移交职位，但杨琦博士接任职位所采用的程序不合常规。由于我担任现职数年，经手案件众多，不可能在短时间内移交所有事务。我从今日起加快移交进度，待我处理完所有事务后，将通知上级派遣官员接管办公室。我不会做任何有害于国家之事。今日杨琦博士前来接管办公室时，由许三郎（Hsu San-long，許三郎）陪同。公众应知许三郎是何等人物。”

高等法院官员发表声明

以下是江苏高等法院第三分院发言人的声明：-

page_data.en:
November 25, 1936. Morning Translation.

"The unfortunate incident between the old and new Presidents of the Shanghai Second Special District Court has arisen because of lack of proper arrangements between the two parties. It is not likely that Mr. Wong Sze-muh will refuse to hand over the post. It is only a question of time. Naturally the High Court is paying attention to this matter and it is possible that it will succeed in making the two Presidents of the District Court come to terms, thereby effecting an amicable solution".

Report Sent to Chungking

Yesterday Dr. Yang Chi made a report to the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court about the removal of his proclamation.. He has sent a telegram to the Ministry of Justice asking for instructions.
At 2 p.m. yesterday the Procuratorate of the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court detailed a Procurator to investigate the removal of the proclamation in order that the matter might be dealt with according to law. Dr. Yang Chi was unable to attend office yesterday afternoon, but the Civil and Criminal Courts of the District Court functioned as usual.

Ta Ying Pao :-

Serious Allegation Against Wong Sze-muh

On November 24, Mr. Wong Sze-muh, the discharged President of the Shanghai Second Special District Court, refused to hand over his office to the new President.
Wong Sze-muh, age 43, native of Chekiang, is a graduate of Paris University. His wife is a French lady. He has been residing in Shanghai for a long time. He is fond of tennis. However, it seems that his nerves are not in proper order for he frequently behaves in an abnormal manner.
In autumn this year, somebody made a complaint against Wong Sze-muh with the Ministry of Justice of the National Government alleging improper action in a certain case. After making an investigation, the Ministry of Justice relieved him of his post. When he called on the French authorities to say farewell, officials of the French authorities, according to custom, expressed regret over his departure. Mistaking this expression of regret as a desire for his retention at the post, Wong decided not to hand over his office. When the new President arrived in Shanghai, many people connected with judicial circles persuaded Wong to hand over his office and the latter agreed to do so. Yesterday, he changed his mind.
According to a report from a reliable source, the private motor car belonging to Wong Sze-muh was noticed recently in front of the New Asia Hotel (新亞酒店), Hongkew, on two occasions. However, persons who are closely connected with Wong say that the car was lent to some French friends of his wife and that Wong had never crossed the bridge into Hongkew.

1936年11月25日。晨间译件。

“上海第二特区地方法院新旧院长之间发生的不幸事件，是由于双方缺乏适当安排所致。王思默先生不太可能拒绝移交职位。这只是时间问题。高等法院自然正在关注此事，并有可能成功促使两位地方法院院长达成妥协，从而实现和平解决”。

发往重庆的报告

昨日，杨琪博士就其公告被撕毁一事向江苏高等法院第三分院作了报告。他已致电司法部请示指示。
昨日下午2时，江苏高等法院第三分院检察处派遣一名检察官调查公告被撕毁一事，以便依法处理此事。杨琪博士昨日下午未能到职办公，但地方法院的民事和刑事法庭照常运作。

《大英报》：

对王思默的严重指控

11月24日，被免职的上海第二特区地方法院院长王思默先生拒绝向新任院长移交办公室。
王思默，43岁，浙江人，毕业于巴黎大学。其妻为法国女士。他长期居住在上海。他喜爱网球。然而，他的神经似乎不太正常，因为他经常行为异常。
今年秋天，有人向国民政府司法部投诉王思默，指控其在某案件中行为不当。经调查后，司法部将其免职。当他拜访法国当局辞行时，法国当局官员按惯例对其离职表示遗憾。王思默误将这种遗憾之辞理解为希望他留任，遂决定不移交办公室。当新任院长抵达上海时，许多司法界人士劝告王思默移交办公室，后者也同意这样做。但昨日，他改变了主意。
据可靠消息来源报道，最近有人两次在虹口新亚酒店前注意到属于王思默的私人汽车。然而，与王思默关系密切的人称，该车是借给他妻子的一些法国朋友的，王思默从未过桥进入虹口。

Dispute Over Court Post
Said Temporarily Settled

The dispute over the office of the Second Special District Court judge reached a temporary settlement yesterday when Judge Yang Chi, the new appointee, was ordered to Chungking by the Minister of Justice, Chinese reports said yesterday.

The dispute arose when Judge Wang Shi-mo, the incumbent judge, refused to give up his post to the incoming judge, his contention being that he had not yet received official notification from the Minister of the dismissal and of the successor.

Meanwhile, it was reported that Judge Wang is winding up his affairs in the court and expects to turn the office over to anyone duly appointed to take over the post.

Judge Yang, the reports said, will leave Shanghai for the war time capital in the near future.

November 29, 1938. Afternoon Translation.

To Ying Yeh Pao dated Nov.28:

THE AFFAIR OF THE SHANGHAI SECOND SPECIAL DISTRICT
COURT

Mr. Wong Sze-muh (王思默), the former
President of the Shanghai Second Special District Court,
is still refusing to hand over his post. After the
Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court had reported to the
Ministry of Justice asking for instructions, the National
Government sent a telegram to Shanghai ordering Wong to
hand over his post at once as ordered.
Upon receiving his appointment from the
Ministry of Justice on November 24, Mr. Yang Chi (楊琪)
came to Shanghai and went to the Shanghai Second Special
District Court to take over the post, but Wong Sze-muh
refused to hand over his duty and tore off the proclamation
issued by the new President announcing his assumption of
office. Upon learning of this, the Third Branch of the
Kiangsu High Court conducted an investigation and made a
report to the National Government asking for instructions.
From enquiries made by a reporter of this
paper among judicial circles, the Ministry of Justice has
sent a telegram to Shanghai ordering Wong Sze-muh to hand
over his post at once. The Third Branch of the Kiangsu
High Court has shown this telegram to Wong Sze-muh.
At noon to-day Wong Sze-muh attended office
as usual, but nothing was done to hand over his post to
the new President.
Certain persons connected with judicial
circles have made the following observations:-
1) The delay to hand over the post is said to be due to
the large number of documents to be cleared up, but the
new President had notified Wong of his arrival some
weeks ago, and he has had sufficient time to make
preparations to hand over his post.
2) If Wong is dissatisfied with the action of the National
Government, he should first hand over his post and take
up the matter with the Government; he should not have
refused to hand over his office.
3) Wong has made certain statements against the new
President - a thing unheard of.
It is said that Wong will hand over his post
if the new President will grant his demands.

11月28日《大英夜报》：

上海第二特区地方法院事件

上海第二特区地方法院前院长王思默先生仍拒绝移交职位。江苏高等法院第三分院向司法部报告并请示指示后，国民政府向上海发出电报，命令王思默按令立即移交职位。
杨琪先生于11月24日收到司法部委任后来到上海，并前往上海第二特区地方法院接管职位，但王思默拒绝移交职务，并撕毁了新任院长宣布就职的公告。江苏高等法院第三分院获悉此事后进行了调查，并向国民政府报告请示指示。
本报记者在司法界 inquiries 得知，司法部已向上海发出电报，命令王思默立即移交职位。江苏高等法院第三分院已向王思默出示了该电报。
今日中午，王思默照常到办公室上班，但未采取任何行动向新任院长移交职位。
司法界某些人士发表了以下看法：
1) 据说移交职位的延误是由于需要清理大量文件，但新任院长已在几周前通知王思默其即将到达，他有足够的时间准备移交职位。
2) 如果王思默对国民政府的行动不满，他应先移交职位，再与政府交涉此事；他不应该拒绝移交办公室。
3) 王思默对新任院长发表了一些言论——这是闻所未闻的。
据说，如果新任院长满足其要求，王思默将移交职位。

November 28, 1938. Afternoon Translation

Crystal (晶報), a mosquito newspaper :-

THE DISPUTE BETWEEN THE OLD AND THE NEW PRESIDENTS OF THE
SHANGHAI SECOND SPECIAL DISTRICT COURT

Mr. Wong Sze-muh (王思默), President of the
Shanghai Second Special District Court, who has held this
position for a number of years, was relieved of his post
last month. He is to be succeeded by Mr. Yang Chi (楊琦),
Chief Procurator of the District Court at Kweichow and
formerly a Procurator of the Shanghai District Court at
Nantao. Thus he is acquainted with conditions in this
locality.

Upon receiving the new appointment, Mr. Yang
came to Shanghai about a fortnight ago but so far he has
not succeeded in taking over the office because Mr. Wong
Sze-muh, the retiring President, has refused to hand over
his duties claiming that he has not yet received instructions
from the Ministry of Justice and further that owing to the
great number of documents it will take him sometime to
settle them.

The other day Mr. Yang together with some of
his men personally called at the Shanghai Second Special
District Court to assume office, but Mr. Wong refused to
see him. In consequence, Mr. Yang secured an interview
with Mr. Sung Shao-kong (孫紹康), the Chief Procurator,
and discussed with him ways and means to settle the affair.
In the course of the conversation, Mr. Sung lent to Mr. Yang
his seal of Chief Procurator with which Mr. Yang issued a
proclamation announcing his assumption of office. This
proclamation was posted at the entrance to the Court
premises by Hsu San-long (許三郎), one of Mr. Yang's
men, who strictly warned the policeman at the gate to look
after the proclamation and to arrest any person, even Mr.
Wong Sze-muh himself, who attempted to remove the procla-
mation. Mr. Yang then left without succeeding in taking
over the office. After Mr. Yang's departure, Mr. Wong
tore off the proclamation.

It is learned that Mr. Yang has reported the
whole affair to the Ministry of Justice asking for
instructions, whereas Mr. Wong, on his part, has given
indications that he will refuse to hand over his duties
and is even making use of the employment of Hsu San-long
by Mr. Yang as an excuse to attack Mr. Yang. It is said
that Hsu San-long had at one time been charged and convicted
of a criminal offence when he was holding the post of Chief
of the Detective Squad (?) of the Shanghai District Court
at Nantao.

小报《晶报》：

上海第二特区地方法院新旧院长之间的争端

担任上海第二特区地方法院院长多年的王思默先生上月被免职。接替他的是杨琦先生，他是贵州地方法院首席检察官，曾任上海南市区地方法院检察官。因此，他熟悉当地情况。

杨琪先生约两周前收到新委任后来到上海，但至今未能接管办公室，因为即将离任的院长王思默先生拒绝移交职务，声称尚未收到司法部的指示，并且由于文件数量庞大，需要一些时间来处理。

日前，杨琪先生与其手下人员亲自前往上海第二特区地方法院就职，但王思默先生拒绝见他。因此，杨琪先生会见了首席检察官孙绍康先生，并与他讨论了解决此事的方法。在谈话过程中，孙先生将他的首席检察官印章借给杨先生，杨先生据此发布公告宣布就职。该公告由杨先生的手下许三郎张贴在法院入口处，许三郎严厉警告门口警察看护好公告，并逮捕任何试图移除公告的人，即使是王思默先生本人。随后，杨先生未能接管办公室便离开了。杨先生离开后，王思默撕毁了公告。

据悉，杨先生已将整个事件报告司法部请示指示，而王思默方面则表明将拒绝移交职务，甚至利用杨先生雇用许三郎一事作为攻击杨先生的借口。据说，许三郎在担任上海南市区地方法院侦探队队长（？）期间，曾因刑事犯罪被起诉并定罪。

CHINA PRESS.

NOV 26 1938

District Judge
Awaits Orders
On Succession

Wang Denies He Refuses
To Yield Post To
New Appointee

Denying that he had refused to turn over his portfolio to a new appointee, Judge Wang Shi-mo, head of the Second Special District Court, told THE CHINA PRESS yesterday that he would do so on receipt of an order from the National Government.

The statement was made in connection with reports circulated yesterday in the vernacular press to the effect that a serious dispute had arisen between Judge Wang and the new appointee, Judge Yang Chi, when the latter attempted to take over the post.

Wang Issues Statement

In his statement, Judge Wang said he had not yet received the order from the National Government.

"As soon as I receive from the Government the order decreeing the new appointment, it will be my duty to turn over my post to the new appointee," Judge Wang said.

Yang Expects Settlement

Meanwhile, representative of Judge Yang, at a press interview, told Chinese newspaper men that "the whole matter will be settled shortly." Judge Yang, he said, does not believe that his predecessor would refuse to turn over his post.

Earlier reports said that when Judge Yang posted an official announcement in front of the court house, informing the public of the appointment, Judge Wang tore down the notice with his own hands.

地方法院法官
等待继任命令

SHANGHAI TIMES,

NOV 25 1936

JUDGES IN DISPUTE
IN FRENCHTOWN

Second District Court
Officials Reported At
Loggerheads

When an ordinary official in
China defies orders from his
superiors it is not news, but when
a chief judge of a court does this,
refusing to hand over his portfolio
to his successor duly appointed by
the Ministry of Justice, it is
something new. This happened in
the Second Special District Court
yesterday when Judge Wang Shi-
mo, the present chief judge, refus-
ed to let his successor Judge Yang
Chi take up his new duties.

It was alleged by Chinese sources
that Judge Yang's first official an-
nouncement stating that he official-
ly took up his duties yesterday,
which was posted in front of
the court building, was torn down
by his predecessor who went
about his routine business as
usual. No official reason was
given by the present chief
judge for his alleged refusal to
carry out the ministerial order.

Besides asking the chief judge of
the Third Branch Kiangsu High
Court in the French Concession
for instructions regarding this
matter, Judge Yang is said to have
also referred the matter to the
Ministry. It would appear that
both sides were determined, but it
is news that the chief judge should
have torn down his successor's
notice with his own hands, if the
Chinese reports are true.

Although no official reason could
be obtained yesterday in regard to
the apparent divergence of opinion
between the two judges, it was
said that for his neglect of office,
as was alleged in a Chinese even-
ing report, Judge Wang's service
as a judicial official had been dis-
continued by the Ministry for two
years. His successor Judge Yang
came here only recently from
Kweichow where he had been the
chief judge of a district court. His
negotiations with the present chief
judge for taking over new duties
proved unsuccessful and yesterday
he asked his assistants to post his
first announcement, disregarding
Judge Wang.

《上海泰晤士报》，

1936年11月25日

法租界法官发生争执

据报道第二特区法院官员
陷入僵局

在中国，一名普通官员违抗上级命令并不算是新闻，但当一名法院首席法官这样做，拒绝将其职权移交给由司法部正式任命的继任者时，这就成了新鲜事。昨天第二特区法院就发生了这样的事，现任首席法官王思默法官拒绝让其继任者杨琪法官履行新职。

据中方消息人士称，杨法官的第一份官方公告声称他已于昨日正式就职，该公告张贴在法院大楼前，被其前任撕毁，而后者则像往常一样处理日常公务。现任首席法官对其据称拒绝执行部令的行为未给出任何官方理由。

据悉，除了就此事向位于法租界的江苏高等法院第三分院首席法官请示外，杨法官还将此事上报至司法部。看来双方都态度坚决，但如果中文报道属实，首席法官亲手撕毁继任者的告示这一消息确属新奇。

虽然昨日未能获得关于两位法官之间明显意见分歧的官方原因，但据称，正如一份中文晚报报道所指出的那样，王法官因玩忽职守，其司法官员任期已被部里中止两年。他的继任者杨法官最近刚从贵州来到这里，他此前曾担任该地区的地方法院首席法官。他与现任首席法官就接管新职进行的谈判证明不成功，昨天他不顾王法官，要求助手张贴了他的第一份公告。

lawyer Chang Fah Yau (張法堯), son of Chang Siao Ling, a
gang leader of Frenchtown, and naturally he is backed up by the

approached the judge who tried the case named Cheu Hwan Ying and
the latter agreed to help. Fearing that this would prove dis-
advantageous to his client, Chang Fah Yau interviewed Wong Sz Muh
the President, and caused the judge to be removed from the case.
